newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices edge higher on cooler forecast.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices edge higher on cooler forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices edged higher Friday as forecasters called for a return to more seasonable temperatures early next week throughout most of the U.S., industry sources said.
Swing Gulf Coast prices were talked in the $2.53-2.60 per mmBtu range, up about three to five cents from Thursday but still more than a $1 under January indices.
Despite well above-normal temperatures now in most of the U.S., the National Weather Service said a cool front moving into the U.S. early next week should push the thermometer to near-normal levels.

Specifically on Transco, a Gulf pipeline delivering gas to the Northeast, prices jumped into the high-$2.60s early, but news that the pipeline would resume normal service later this afternoon on its Alabama lateral put downward pressure on the market.
At the New York city-gate, prices ranged anywhere from $3.25 to $3.70, little changed from Thursday's levels.
Temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic states are expected to remain above-normal through the weekend but then gradually cool to near-normal by Wednesday.

In the Appalachian region, prices on Columbia Gas were talked in the $2.75-2.80 range early, but shortly before nomination deadlines buyers were bidding for gas in the $2.90s. On CNG, prices were in the low-$3 area, traders said.
Midcontinent prices were also up about five cents to the $2.30-2.40 range on cooler weather prospects.

Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to remain well above-normal through Saturday, but the arrival of a cool front late Saturday will push temperatures down to near-normal levels by early next week.

In west Texas, where temperatures are expected to cool to about five to 20 degrees above-normal and then return to near-normal Monday and Tuesday, Permian gas prices gained almost five cents to the low-$3.30s.
At the southern border, prices were up about 10 cents to the $2.40-2.65 range, with most deals reported done around $2.50.
